intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: The tide has turned. Every rope tied along the edge hangs at a new angle.

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “Everything has moved since we last spoke. The eddy by the wall is gone. There is a new one by your foot.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “It means I get a new place twice a day without the trouble of moving house.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “Surface people move once a decade and complain about it for a year.”

options.labelText: “So where’s the good current now? Quiz me.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “Very well. Point to where you would swim.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: You point at the calmest patch of water. She points, with great patience, at the patch beside it.

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “Close. Yours would have taken you very politely out to sea.”

options.labelText: “You could pick one route and stick to it. Less to keep track of.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “Then the tide turns, and my route goes straight into the wall.”
